title: Screenshots are context too
body: You can attach an image to a chat prompt and ask questions about it, such as a UI bug or a diagram. You can even drag an image straight from a web browser onto the Chat view.

title: Hand over a page element
body: In VS Code’s integrated browser, Add Element to Chat attaches the selected HTML element with its CSS styles and a screenshot. Add Console Logs to Chat attaches runtime errors as well.

title: Steer a running request
body: You don’t have to wait or cancel. While Copilot is working, you can queue a follow-up, steer it once the current tool finishes, or stop it and send your new message straight away.

title: Alt text from the lightbulb
body: On a Markdown image link, the lightbulb offers Generate alt text, or Refine alt text if the image already has some. An easy accessibility win for READMEs and docs.

title: Checkpoints are not Git
body: Restore Checkpoint rewinds files and chat history to before a request. It can’t undo terminal commands, network requests or deployments the agent has already run, so keep committing as normal.

title: Rewrite an earlier prompt
body: You can edit any request in a chat. Change an earlier prompt and VS Code reverts the file changes from that request and every later one, so you can retry with a better prompt.

title: Chat in its own window
body: Run Chat: New Chat Window to give chat a window of its own, handy on a second monitor. Chat: New Chat Editor opens it as an editor tab, so you can compare sessions side by side.

title: Debug by adding a prefix
body: Put copilot-debug in front of your usual run command, for example copilot-debug python foo.py, and VS Code starts a debugging session for it. The feature is in preview.

title: Shared context with Spaces
body: Copilot Spaces gather repos, issues, PRs, notes and uploaded files as context for Copilot. You can share organisation spaces with colleagues, and GitHub sources update automatically when they change.

title: MCP servers run code
body: An MCP server gives the agent new tools, but the docs warn that local MCP servers can run arbitrary code on your machine. Only install servers from sources you trust.

title: Ask why CI failed
body: On a pull request on GitHub, open the menu beside a failing check and choose Explain error. Copilot Chat opens with the failed workflow as context and may suggest a fix.

title: Help with merge conflicts
body: Open a file with conflicts and select Resolve Merge Conflict with AI. The agent uses the merge base and both branches’ changes to propose a resolution for you to review. It is experimental.
